source_text: Ἐχρῆν δὲ αὐτὸν, εἴπερ εὐγνωμόνει πρὸς τὴν κατηγορίαν, ἐκθέσθαι αὐταῖς λέξεσι τὰς προφητείας, εἴτ᾿ ἐν αἷς θεὸς παντοκράτωρ ἐπηγγέλλετο εἶναι ὁ λέγων, εἴτ᾿ ἐν αἷς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, εἴτε καὶ ἐν αἷς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον λέγον εἶναι ἐπιστεύετο· οὕτω γὰρ καὶ ἠγωνίασεν ἀνασκευάσαι τὰ εἰρημένα καὶ δεῖξαι ὅτι οὐκ ἔνθεοι ἦσαν οἱ λόγοι, περιέχοντες ἐπιστροφὴν ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων καὶ ἔλεγχον τῶν ποτε ὄντων καὶ πρόγνωσιν περὶ τῶν μελλόντων. διὸ καὶ οἱ κατ᾿ αὐτοὺς ἀπογραψάμενοι τὰς προφητείας αὐτῶν ἐφύλαξαν, ἵνα καὶ οἱ μεταγενέστεροι ἀναγινώσκοντες θαυμάζωσιν ὡς λόγους θεοῦ καὶ ὠφελούμενοι οὐ μόνον ἀπὸ τῶν ἐπιπληκτικῶν καὶ ἐπιστρεπτικῶν ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν προγνωστικῶν ταῖς ἐκβάσεσι πειθόμενοι περὶ τοῦ θεῖον εἶναι πνεῦμα τὸ προειρηκὸς τὴν κατὰ τὸν λόγον εὐσέβειαν ἀσκοῦντες διατελῶσι, πειθόμενοι τῷ νόμῳ καὶ τοῖς προφήταις. οἱ μὲν ουν προφῆται ὅσα ἦν αὐτόθεν νοηθῆναι τοῖς ἀκούουσι χρήσιμα καὶ συμβαλλόμενα τῇ τῶν ἠθῶν ἐπανορθώσει χωρὶς πάσης ἐπικρύψεως κατὰ τὸ βούλημα τοῦ θεοῦ εἰρήκασιν, ὅσα δὲ μυστικώτερα ἦν καὶ ἐποπτικώτερα καὶ ἐχόμενα θεωρίας τῆς ὑπὲρ τὴν πάνδημον ἀκοὴν, ταῦτα „δι᾿ αἰνιγμάτων“ καὶ ἀλληγοριῶν καὶ τῶν καλουμένων σκοτεινῶν λόγων καὶ τῶν ὀνομαζομένων παραβολῶν ἢ παροιμιῶν ἀπεφήναντο· ἵν᾿ οἱ μὴ φυγοπονοῦντες ἀλλὰ πάντα πόνον ὑπὲρ ἀρετῆς καὶ ἀληθείας ἀναδεχόμενοι ἐξετάσαντες εὕρωσι καὶ εὑρόντες, ὡς λόγος αἱρεῖ, οἰκονομήσωσιν. ὁ δὲ γεννάδας Κέλσος ὡσπερεὶ θυμωθεὶς ἐπὶ τῷ μὴ νενοηκέναι τοὺς τῶν προφητῶν τοιούτους λόγους ἐλοιδόρησεν αὐτοὺς, εἰπὼν ὅτι ταῦτα ἐπανατεινάμενοι προστιθέασιν ἐφεξῆς ἄγνωστα καὶ πάροιστρα καὶ πάντῃ ἄδηλα, ὧν τὸ μὲν γνῶμα οὐδεὶς ἂν νοῦν ἔχων εὑρεῖν δύναιτο· ἀσαφῆ γὰρ καὶ τὸ μηδὲν, ἀνοήτῳ δὲ ἢ γόητι παντὶ περὶ παντὸς ἀφορμὴν ἐνδίδωσιν, ὅπῃ βούλεται, τὸ λεχθὲν σφετερίζεσθαι. καὶ πανούργως μοι ἔδοξε ταῦτ᾿ εἰρηκέναι, κωλύειν τὸ ὅσον ἐφ᾿ ἑαυτῷ βουλόμενος τοὺς ἐντυγχάνοντας ταῖς προφητείαις βασανίζειν καὶ ἐξετάζειν αὐτῶν τὸν νοῦν· καὶ πέπονθέ τι πρᾶγμα παραπλήσιον τοῖς εἰποῦσι περί τινος προφήτου, εἰσελθόντος πρός τινα καὶ τὰ μέλλοντα προειπόντος αὐτῷ· „τί εἰσῆλθεν ὁ ἐπίληπτος οὗτος πρός σε;“
pass_a_gloss: But it was necessary for him, if he was well-disposed towards the accusation, to set out the prophecies in the same words, whether in those in which God Almighty was promising to be the one speaking, or in those in which the Son of God was, or even in those in which the Holy Spirit was believed to be speaking; for in this way he also contended to dismantle the things that were said and to show that the words were not inspired, containing a turning away from sins and a rebuke of what once was and a foreknowledge of what is to come. Therefore, those who copied down the prophecies of the prophets also preserved them, so that those who come later, reading them, might marvel at them as words of God and, being benefited not only from the reproachful and corrective ones but also from the predictive ones, might be persuaded by the outcomes to be about the divine spirit, practicing piety according to the word, being persuaded by the law and the prophets. The prophets, then, said whatever was useful for those hearing to think and contributing to the correction of character, without any concealment, according to the will of God; but whatever was more mystical and more contemplative and having a theory beyond common hearing, these things they declared through riddles and allegories and what are called dark sayings and the so-called parables or proverbs; so that those not shirking labor but receiving all labor for virtue and truth, having examined, might find and, having found, as reason chooses, might manage. But the foolish Celsus, as if being angry because he did not understand the prophets' such words, insulted them, saying that they, stretching out these things, add in sequence unknown and absurd and completely unclear things, of which no one, having a mind, would be able to find the meaning; for they are unclear and meaningless, and they give an opportunity to any foolish or deceitful person to interpret whatever they want, wherever they want; and I think he said these things cunningly, to prevent those who wish to examine the prophecies from testing and examining their mind; and he suffered something similar to those who said something about a certain prophet, who entered to someone and foretold the future to him: 'Why did this epileptic enter to you?'

choices.why: the verb εὐγνωμονέω means to be favorably inclined
the word παντοκράτωρ is a title for God
the verb ἐπαγγέλλω means to promise
the word ἐπίληπτος means suffering from epilepsy

pass_b_english: If he had been well-disposed toward the accusation, he ought to have set out the prophecies in their own words — whether those in which God Almighty promised to be the speaker, or those in which the Son of God was the speaker, or even those in which the Holy Spirit was believed to be speaking. For in this way he also struggled to dismantle what had been said and to show that the words were not inspired, even though they contain a turning away from sins, a rebuke of what once was, and a foreknowledge of what is to come. That is why those who copied down the prophecies of the prophets also preserved them, so that later readers might marvel at them as words of God and be benefited not only by the reproachful and corrective passages but also by the predictive ones. By the outcomes they are persuaded concerning the divine Spirit, and so they continue practicing piety according to the word, persuaded by the law and the prophets. The prophets spoke whatever was useful for hearers to understand and that contributed to the correction of character, without any concealment, according to the will of God. But whatever was more mystical, more contemplative, and belonged to a theory beyond common hearing, they declared through riddles, allegories, what are called dark sayings, and the so-called parables or proverbs — so that those who do not shirk labor but accept every toil for the sake of virtue and truth, after examining, might find, and having found, might manage as reason directs. But the foolish Celsus, as if enraged because he did not grasp such words of the prophets, insulted them. He said that, stretching these things out, they add in sequence unknown, absurd, and completely unclear things, of which no one with a mind could find the meaning. For they are unclear and meaningless, and they give any foolish or deceitful person an opportunity to interpret whatever they want, wherever they want. And it seemed to me he said these things cunningly, wishing to prevent those who encounter the prophecies from testing and examining their meaning, as far as he is able. He suffered something similar to those who spoke about a certain prophet: when a prophet entered someone's presence and foretold the future to him, they said, "Why did this epileptic enter to you?"
